description: This is a false-colour satellite image depicting marshes and an estuary of the Guadalquivir river within the Doñana Natura 2000 (N2K) site in Spain. The image was captured by the Spot 5 satellite at a 2.5 metre (m) resolution on 2011-08-01, using a 1/2/3 band combination. The dominant features are extensive areas of intense red, arranged in large, mostly rectangular, geometrically segmented plots. These red hues typically indicate actively vegetated marshland or areas within salt pans (salines) containing photosynthetic organisms in a false-colour infrared composite. The large red plots are separated by thin, lighter-coloured linear features, likely representing embankments, paths, or bare ground. A curving, lighter brown/tan area is visible in the lower central part, representing an estuary or river channel, with adjacent lighter, irregular patches that could be mudflats or bare soil. Scattered darker patches within the red areas may indicate open water bodies or less vegetated zones. The image credit is CNES 2011©, Distribution Airbus DS/Spot Image.
